title: Late-expiratory volume fraction does not improve transported wheeze prediction beyond standard spirometry
abstract: We tested whether 1-FEV3/FEV6 adds wheeze information beyond demographics, smoking, FEV1, FVC, FEV1/FVC and FEF25-75. Separately recruited NHANES2007-2008 and2009-2010 survey datasets supplied 3563 training and 3959 target adults with acceptable volume quality and expirations lasting at least6seconds. Weighted frozen logistic models yielded target Brier 0.0937933 versus 0.0938352; delta +0.0000419, conditional target-PSU95% interval [-0.0001132,+0.0001959], joint-refit interval [-0.0001130,+0.0005448]. AUC delta was -0.001587. No reliable incremental improvement was demonstrated. This is an incremental-prediction test of an established physiological index, not a new biomarker or causal inference. Related prior analyses exposed survey covariates; the temporal transport test is not untouched independent clinical-cohort validation.
